source: TomorrowX Summit (iConnections) — Opening session: retail as most powerful market force, AI buildout railroad vs telecom, P(doom) vs P(boom)
summary: Value of compute will continue to rise if AI continues to become more economically useful; elasticity of token demand is the key variable
summary_extended: Baker argues that the central question for AI infrastructure investing is whether the elasticity of token demand remains positive — meaning, as the cost of tokens falls, does total demand for tokens rise fast enough to keep aggregate compute spending growing? If the answer is yes, the value of compute continues to rise and the AI buildout continues unabated, analogous to the railroad buildout rather than the telecom overbuild. He frames value as accruing across a five-layer stack: LAN/power, multiple chip types (not just GPUs), compute, networking, memory, and storage — suggesting the opportunity is broader than any single component. The investment implication is to remain long AI infrastructure broadly, but the thesis is explicitly conditional and Baker does not assert certainty, making it a framework for monitoring rather than a high-conviction directional call.
detail: Baker frames 'is the elasticity of token demand still positive?' as the central question. If yes, compute value rises and the buildout continues. The value accrues across the five-layer stack: LAN/power, different chip types, compute vs. networking vs. memory vs. storage.
